title: Krkonoše — Špindlerův Mlýn, Pec and the Ridge Tour

bestPeriod.note: The ridge above 1,300 m holds a reliable base longest; valley snow at Špindlerův Mlýn is now heavily snowmaking-dependent by comparison.

summary: A week skiing Špindlerův Mlýn and Pec pod Sněžkou, with a guided ski-touring day on the Krkonoše ridge and the national park's real winter access closures explained.
hook: Krkonoše is not the Alps, and it does not try to be — the whole range tops out at 1,603 m, at Sněžka. What it has instead is a genuinely wild, wind-scoured summit ridge, two well-built but not-quite-connected valley resorts, and a national park administration that closes large parts of the high ground every winter to protect it. This week skis both valley resorts, respects the closures, and spends one day on the ridge itself with a certified guide.

snapshot.Base(s): Špindlerův Mlýn (5 nights), Pec pod Sněžkou (2 nights)
snapshot.Best Period: January–March; the ridge holds snow longest, valley slopes are snowmaking-supported
snapshot.Total Distance / Terrain: Base approx. 715 m (Špindlerův Mlýn), top approx. 1,603 m (Sněžka, ridge tour only); resort lift-served terrain tops around 1,235–1,299 m
snapshot.Getting There: Fly to Prague (PRG); bus or shared shuttle to Špindlerův Mlýn, roughly 2h30
snapshot.Who It Suits: Intermediate skiers who want a lower-key, lower-cost Central European week, plus anyone keen to try ski touring on gentle, well-marked terrain

itinerary.title: Arrival and Medvědín
itinerary.morning: Bus from Prague's Florenc station to Špindlerův Mlýn, arriving into the town at 715 m, wedged along the young Elbe (Labe) river at the foot of two separate ski mountains.
itinerary.afternoon: Ride the Medvědín gondola on the north side of the valley for an orientation lap — Medvědín's runs are broad, mostly red-graded, and reliably snowmaking-covered from top to bottom.
itinerary.evening: Walk the short riverside street; Špindlerův Mlýn is small enough to see in twenty minutes, and most restaurants sit within that stretch.
itinerary.dayStats: approx. 700 m vertical · Medvědín sector · 2 lift hours.

itinerary.title: Svatý Petr and the interconnect that isn't
itinerary.morning: Cross the valley — literally, since Medvědín and the Svatý Petr/Hromovka sector on the opposite mountain are not lift-connected. This is the week's first honest interconnect lesson: Špindlerův Mlýn markets itself as one resort, but skiing between its two halves means riding down to the valley floor and taking the free ski bus (or a ten-minute walk in good conditions) rather than a direct lift.
itinerary.afternoon: Svatý Petr's slopes, served by a modern gondola from town, include the FIS-graded Svatý Petr race piste, one of the steeper pitches in the Czech resort scene, plus gentler blues off to the side for a mixed-ability group.
itinerary.evening: Dinner in town; the bus link between the two sectors stops running by early evening, so plan any sector-hopping for daylight hours.
itinerary.dayStats: approx. 3,600 m vertical · Svatý Petr/Hromovka sector · 4 lift hours.

itinerary.title: National park boundaries and a low-key touring intro
itinerary.morning: The Krkonoše National Park (KRNAP) enforces a genuinely strict winter access regime: large sections of the highest ground, including most of the main ridge above the tree line, sit in Zone I, the strict nature reserve, where travel off marked and specifically winter-permitted routes is prohibited, and several connecting ridge paths are closed outright from 1 November to 31 May to protect overwintering chamois and capercaillie. This is enforced by park rangers, not a suggestion — check the current KRNAP winter route map at the Špindlerova bouda information point before planning any ridge walking or touring.
itinerary.afternoon: Take an introductory ski-touring lesson on the permitted, gentle terrain near Labská bouda, reached by a marked winter route from the top of the Medvědín lift system. This is the low-commitment version of tomorrow's bigger day: skins, touring bindings, and a guide explaining how the park's permitted-route system works before anyone commits to the full ridge.
itinerary.evening: Early dinner; tomorrow's ridge day starts early.
itinerary.dayStats: approx. 400 m vertical touring · Labská bouda approach, permitted route · half-day.

itinerary.title: Guided day on the Krkonoše ridge
itinerary.morning: Book a full guided ski-touring day through a certified guide from the Asociace horských vůdců ČR (the Czech Mountain Guides Association), which trains and certifies guides who legally operate within the park's permitted winter corridors. A guide here is the practical way to use the ridge's permitted routes correctly and read conditions on genuinely exposed, wind-loaded terrain that looks deceptively gentle from below.
itinerary.afternoon: A typical route runs from Labská bouda along the permitted ridge section toward Luční bouda, with wide views into Poland on the border ridge; the guide checks the daily avalanche bulletin from Horská služba ČR (the Czech Mountain Rescue Service), rated on the standard five-level European avalanche danger scale (1 Low to 5 Very High), before committing — wind slab on the exposed ridge is the real hazard here, not steep-slope avalanche terrain in the alpine sense.
itinerary.evening: Return to Špindlerův Mlýn; a guided ridge day in genuinely raw weather is tiring even on gentle gradients, and an early night is standard.
itinerary.dayStats: approx. 12 km, 500 m vertical touring · Krkonoše main ridge, permitted corridor · full guided day.

itinerary.title: Transfer to Pec pod Sněžkou
itinerary.morning: Bus or taxi transfer over to Pec pod Sněžkou, on the eastern side of the range and the base for the Sněžka cable car. Check into Pec and ski the afternoon on the Hnědý vrch sector directly above town.
itinerary.afternoon: Pec's slopes, part of the larger SkiResort Černá hora–Pec network that also links Zahrádky and, via ski bus rather than direct lift, the separate Černá hora mountain above Janské Lázně, are gentler on average than Špindlerův Mlýn's, which makes this a good rest-legs day after the touring effort.
itinerary.evening: Pec's small centre sits directly below Sněžka, Czechia's highest peak (1,603 m) and the border ridge with Poland — worth a look up at the summit weather station even from the valley floor.
itinerary.dayStats: approx. 2,400 m vertical · Hnědý vrch sector · 3 lift hours.

itinerary.title: Černá hora and the honest snow check
itinerary.morning: Take the ski bus over to Janské Lázně and ride the Černá hora cable car, a modern gondola that replaced the Czech Republic's historic first chairlift, up to the summit area near 1,299 m. Černá hora sits slightly higher and more sheltered than either Špindlerův Mlýn sector, and in a marginal-snow year this is genuinely the more reliable of the three main areas.
itinerary.afternoon: This is the trip's honest bad-snow plan B in practice: if the valley base at Špindlerův Mlýn or Pec has looked thin earlier in the week, weight the second half of the trip toward Černá hora's higher runs rather than the lower-altitude sectors, and treat any run below about 900 m as conditional on the week's actual snow report rather than assumed.
itinerary.evening: Return to Pec for a final evening; the walk around the small town centre, with views up to Sněžka, is a good way to close the trip.
itinerary.dayStats: approx. 3,000 m vertical · Černá hora sector · 4 lift hours.

itinerary.title: Last morning and departure
itinerary.morning: A final short session on Pec's Zahrádky sector, quieter than Hnědý vrch and a gentle way to end the week.
itinerary.afternoon: Return skis, and take the bus back toward Prague, allowing a comfortable buffer — the Pec–Prague road route runs through smaller towns and can be slow in winter weather.
itinerary.dayStats: approx. 1,400 m vertical · Zahrádky sector · 2 lift hours.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotel Start
accommodationStrategy.description: A straightforward hotel a short walk from both the Medvědín gondola and the Svatý Petr shuttle bus stop, useful given the two sectors' lack of direct lift connection.
accommodationStrategy.booking: six weeks ahead for peak February weeks.

accommodationStrategy.name: Horský hotel Krakonoš
accommodationStrategy.description: Sits directly at the base of the Hnědý vrch lifts in Pec, with ski storage and an easy walk to the Sněžka cable-car connection point in Janské Lázně's direction.
accommodationStrategy.priceNote: €65–€100 per night for two, often half board

accommodationStrategy.name: Labská bouda
accommodationStrategy.description: A working mountain hut directly on the plateau near the touring route used on Day 3 and Day 4; staying a night here (rather than commuting up each day) suits anyone wanting an early start on the guided ridge tour.
accommodationStrategy.booking: three weeks ahead; beds are limited and often taken by touring groups.
accommodationStrategy.priceNote: €45–€75 per night for two, half board typical

logistics.connectivity: Reliable in both resort towns; drops out fast on the open ridge, which the guide accounts for with radio and offline maps — do not rely on phone signal above the tree line.
logistics.emergency: 112 pan-European; mountain rescue in the Krkonoše is handled by Horská služba ČR, reachable via 112 or the regional line posted at every lift base.
logistics.bookingWindows: Czech school holiday weeks (staggered by region through February) sell out both resorts; check the specific week against the holiday calendar before booking.
logistics.money: Czechia uses the koruna (CZK); cards are widely accepted, but smaller mountain huts, including Labská bouda, often prefer cash.

other.label: Emergencies
other.text: 112 pan-European; mountain rescue in the Krkonoše is handled by Horská služba ČR, reachable via 112 or the regional line posted at every lift base.

other.label: National park rules
other.text: Off-route travel in KRNAP's Zone I is illegal, and rangers do check; the permitted winter corridor system exists so guided and independent skiers can still use the ridge responsibly. Confirm the current permitted-route map before any touring day.

other.label: Opening-hour traps
other.text: The inter-sector ski bus in Špindlerův Mlýn runs a reduced-frequency winter timetable — check current times rather than assuming an Alpine-style continuous shuttle.

other.label: Avalanche equipment
other.text: Mandatory for the ridge tour: transceiver, probe and shovel, generally supplied and checked by the guide association's outfitters — confirm when booking.

proTips: Ski Medvědín in the morning and Svatý Petr in the afternoon on a clear day, rather than trying to bounce between them more than once — the bus transfer eats real time.
Book the guided ridge day for the clearest forecast window in the week, even if it means shuffling the itinerary; the ridge in poor visibility is a washout regardless of snow quality.
Černá hora is consistently the least crowded of the three main areas on a weekday — worth weighting toward it if Špindlerův Mlýn or Pec feel busy.
The Sněžka summit weather station and the short walk up from the top of the Pec-side lifts (in good visibility only) gives a view into Poland that most week-long visitors skip entirely.
Czech ski school and guide pricing runs well below equivalent Austrian or Swiss rates — a genuinely good-value place to try touring for the first time.
Buy multi-day lift tickets covering both Špindlerův Mlýn's sectors together; the combined ticket is cheaper than paying per sector per day.

packingNotes: Transceiver, probe and shovel for the ridge touring day.
Touring bindings or a rental set booked in advance at Labská bouda or in Špindlerův Mlýn — stock is limited outside the main resort towns.
A windproof shell rated for genuinely raw exposed-ridge conditions; the Krkonoše ridge is famous locally for wind, not cold in isolation.
Layers that adapt between snowmaking-groomed valley runs and the more variable natural snow on the ridge.
Cash in koruna for mountain huts and the ski bus if it is not card-enabled.
A map or offline GPS track of the current KRNAP permitted winter routes.
whatCouldGoWrong: **Valley snow is thin at Špindlerův Mlýn.** Fallback: weight the week toward Černá hora's higher, more sheltered runs, already scheduled for the second half.
**Poor visibility cancels the ridge tour.** Fallback: reschedule it for the last clear day, and use the freed day for an extra session at Pec.
**The inter-sector ski bus runs late or crowded.** Fallback: ski one sector fully in the morning and commit to it for the afternoon rather than chasing a tight connection.
**A booked hut bed on the ridge falls through.** Fallback: base the touring day from the valley instead — an early start, but no overnight needed.
